rem:collatz-three-forms:
Remark Three faces of the q-Collatz conjecture. The contact boundary (conj:collatz-contact-boundary) establishes that the q-Collatz orbit contracts if and only if each tripling is followed by at least two halvings on average. This condition has equivalent categorical, arithmetic, and residue faces.

In the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q), the Collatz step composes Hecke reduction (T^2 = (q-q^{-1})T + 1) and Markov destabilization (\mathrm{tr}_M(xT_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x)). The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_n(q) \to \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] sends braid words to Jones polynomials.

The categorical conjecture asserts that for every h \in H_n(q), the iterated Markov trace converges to the unknot:

\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\mathcal{C}_q^k(h)\bigr) \xrightarrow{k \to \infty} 1.

The identity braid is the unique attractor of the Hecke--Collatz dynamics. Every braid untangles to the unknot under iterated crossing resolution and destabilization.

The contact boundary translates this into a divisibility condition on the Skein module \mathcal{S}(q) \cong \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]. Each odd step produces [3]_q P + 1. The Skein divisibility identity [3]_q = q[2]_q + 1 guarantees one built-in halving. The net contraction per cycle with v total halvings is [3]_q / [2]_q^v. This is contractive if and only if [2]_q^v > [3]_q. The integer threshold is exactly v = 2. Two halvings per tripling are required.

The [2]_q-divisor is q = -1. Evaluating the Collatz output at this divisor: since [3]_q|_{q=-1} = 1 and [2]_q|_{q=-1} = 0, the condition v_{[2]} \geq 2 becomes (q+1)^2-divisibility of [3]_q P + 1 at q = -1.

At q = 1 (the classical limit), the expected 2-adic valuation of 3n+1 for uniformly distributed odd n is:

\mathbb{E}[v_2(3n+1)] = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} k \cdot 2^{-k} = 2.

The classical Collatz conjecture lives at the critical threshold where the average number of halvings per tripling exactly equals the minimum needed. There is no margin.

For q > 1, the algebraic gap [2]_q^2 - [3]_q = q > 1 provides positive margin. However, q = 1 is a torsion point (\mu_1) where the QOU axioms fail. The classical hardness of Collatz reflects this torsion degeneration: the gap collapses to q = 1, the margin vanishes, and individual orbits might fail. The conjecture asserts they never do.
rem:q-collatz-interpretation:
Remark Skein-Collatz interpretation: the (p_1^{k_1}, p_2^{k_2}) family and uniqueness of (2,3). The q-Collatz conjecture (conj:q-collatz) lives in the Skein module \mathcal{S}(q) \cong \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}].

Identity Formula Role
Skein divisibility [3]_q = q[2]_q + 1 "3n+1 is even for odd n"
Contraction gap [2]_q^2 - [3]_q = q Two halvings beat one tripling
Hecke reduction T^2 = (q-q^{-1})T + 1 Crossing words reduce

The Skein relation rewrites as:

J(L_+) = q^{-2}J(L_-) + (1-q^{-2})J(L_0).

For q > 1, this is a convex combination. Crossing resolution is non-expansive on Jones polynomial values.

The Collatz map (2, 3) belongs to a family of generalized maps (p_1, p_2). The q-deformed contraction condition requires k_1 halvings to overpower k_2 triplings:

[p_1]_q^{k_1} > [p_2]_q^{k_2}.

The contraction gap [p_1]_q^{k_1} - [p_2]_q^{k_2} determines the contraction regime.

At the classical boundary p_1^{k_1} = p_2^{k_2} + 1, the q-gap polynomial may develop negative high-degree coefficients:

(p_1^{k_1}, p_2^{k_2}) Classical gap q-gap All q > 0?
(2^2, 3^1) — Collatz 4 - 3 = 1 q Yes (monomial)
(3^2, 8^1) 9 - 8 = 1 q + 2q^2 + q^3 - q^5 - q^6 - q^7 No
(4^2, 15^1) 16 - 15 = 1 negative high-degree terms No

Collatz (2^2, 3^1) is the unique critical case where the q-gap is a monomial. The identity [2]_q^2 - [3]_q = q produces a gap with a single term q, positive for all q > 0. Every other critical case produces a gap polynomial with negative terms that dominate for large q.

Proved results:

  • [3]_q = q[2]_q + 1
  • [2]_q^2 - [3]_q = q
  • [3]_q < [2]_q^2 for q > 0
  • \sqrt{[3]_q/[2]_q^2} < 1
  • (3, 4) gap positive for q > 0
  • (3, 8) gap fails for q > 2

The orbit structure provides the two halvings. The [2]_q-adic valuation of \mathcal{C}_q(P) must average to at least 2 (contact boundary). At q = 1, this average is exactly 2. The conjecture asserts this holds for all q > 1.
rem:collatz-surreal-bound:
Remark Surreal bound for Collatz: contact-boundary deviation costs transfinite Reeb period. This translates the contact-boundary argument of the q-Collatz conjecture (q-Collatz, Collatz no cycles) into a literal surreal inequality in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon).

Let \varepsilon \in \mathrm{Der}(A) be the Reeb infinitesimal (Reeb infinitesimal) and q = 1 + \varepsilon (q from \varepsilon). The q-Collatz conjecture translates the integer orbit into a skein-module resolution on the Reeb contact boundary. A rogue orbit is a non-trivial cycle or an unbounded hailstone. The rogue drift \delta measures the excess contact volume produced per step.

The Reeb period of the contact boundary is \Omega_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-1} (surreal rate calculus). A standard-real drift \delta > 0 per step produces an accumulated contact-volume deviation over one Reeb period:

V(\delta) \asymp \delta^2 \cdot \Omega_q \asymp \delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon^{-1}

The mass-gap dissipation available to re-absorb the deviation is \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3. By surreal squeeze, \delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon^{-1} > \varepsilon^3 strictly in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon). Hence:

V(\delta) > \Delta_q \qquad (\text{in } \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon) \subset \mathbf{No}).

Equivalently, \ordw(V(\delta)) = 1 > -3 = \ordw(\Delta_q) in the \omega-adic order of Big-O via \ordw.

No rogue orbit with standard-real drift \delta > 0 can persist. The Reeb period sweeps a contact-volume transfinite larger than the mass-gap infinitesimal. No budget exists to dissipate the accumulated excess. This is the surreal-arithmetic form of the q-Collatz conjecture, consistent with Collatz no cycles.

The classical Collatz orbit on \mathbb{N} is the standard part \mathrm{st}\bigl(\cdot \,|_{q = 1 + \varepsilon}\bigr) of the q-deformed skein resolution (calculus up to \varepsilon). Every infinitesimal drift vanishes under \mathrm{st}. Every standard-real drift is prohibited by the squeeze above. Therefore, \mathrm{st}(\delta) = 0 for every admissible surreal drift. All orbits terminate at 1.

The q-Collatz statement upgrades to a surreal inequality that rules out all standard-real drifts. The classical conjecture is recovered only by assuming the q-Collatz skein-module resolution admits a well-defined standard part.
rem:surreal-bounds-graded-mikusinski:
Remark Surreal-bound family as graded-Mikusiński std-collapse instances. The four millennium-problem surreal bounds (Surreal bound for Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer: rank--order matches \omega-order of L-series, Surreal bound for the Riemann hypothesis: why \delta = 0 on the critical line, Surreal bound for P vs NP: Reeb-period transfinite exceeds classical-budget standard, Surreal bound for Collatz: contact-boundary deviation costs transfinite Reeb period) share a structural mechanism. The standard-part map \mathrm{std} \colon \mathbf{No} \to \mathbb{R} collapses a transfinite cost on the surreal-envelope side to a standard-real cost on the archimedean side, leaving a finite gap. Per Surreal squeeze: standard-scale cost dominates infinitesimal dissipation, the gap forces the inequality.

The graded-Mikusiński correspondence (GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence) identifies these four remarks as the same construction at different depths of the iterated-integral filtration on \mathcal{H}_q:

Bound Conjecture interpreted Depth class Std-collapsed object
RH Collapse of the quantum gap \mathcal{P}_1 (logs) \zeta critical-line vanishing
BSD The q-deformed Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture \mathcal{P}_2 (regulators) L-function rank match
P vs NP P vs NP in the QOU: classical-limit separation of BQP-width classes \mathcal{P}_{\geq 1} (transfinite Reeb period) budget separation
Collatz The q-Collatz conjecture: Skein-module crossing resolution \mathcal{P}_2 (Bloch–Wigner shadow) contact-boundary deviation

The depth assignment above is conjectural modulo GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence. The correspondence generates all four bounds via the single form:

\mathrm{std}\!\left( \text{depth-}n \text{ infinitesimal cost in } \mathbf{No} \right) > \text{standard archimedean budget},

where n ranges over the four classes and \mathrm{std} serves as the archimedean realization. The inequality direction is enforced by Surreal squeeze: standard-scale cost dominates infinitesimal dissipation.

Unifying the four bounds provides three concrete consequences. First, problem-specific squeezes are replaced with a universal std-collapse at a specified depth, analogous to Mikusiński's (1959) field of fractions unifying operational identities. Second, closing the squeeze at depth n for one millennium problem transports to any other problem at the same depth (e.g., depth-2 techniques for BSD \leftrightarrow Collatz). Third, the correspondence predicts a depth-3 surreal bound for any open problem whose archimedean reading involves weight-3 Goncharov periods (multiple zeta values \zeta(3), \zeta(2,1)), such as Apéry-style irrationality questions (Zagier 1986). For orientation on that programme: for every odd a \geq 3, \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} \mathrm{span}\{1, \zeta(3), \zeta(5), \ldots, \zeta(a)\} > 0.395 \log a [zudilin2001, Thm. 4]. This bounds a dimension; it does not decide the irrationality of any single \zeta(2k+1) with k \geq 2.

This relates to graded Titchmarsh. Mikusiński passes from C[0,\infty) to its field of fractions via Titchmarsh's no-zero-divisor theorem. The graded analog asks at which iterated-integral depth the *_q-product on \mathcal{H}_q first acquires zero divisors. Each surreal-bound remark is an obstruction to inverting a depth-n element, representing exactly the obstruction Mikusiński removes by passing to fractions. The four bounds are instances of graded Titchmarsh failure, each occurring at its characteristic depth.

The novel mathematical content resides in GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence and its discharge targets.
rem:millennium-unification:
Remark Millennium problems unified by the surreal squeeze \delta^2 / \varepsilon > \varepsilon^3. Six classical-limit problems tackled by the QOU framework (the Riemann hypothesis, 3D Navier--Stokes regularity, Collatz, P vs NP, Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer, and the Yang--Mills mass gap) reduce to a single surreal inequality between the cost of a standard-real deviation and the mass-gap infinitesimal. The adelic--Tate factorisation provides the local-global refinement.

Let \varepsilon \in \mathrm{Der}(A) be the Reeb infinitesimal (Reeb infinitesimal) and q = 1 + \varepsilon (q from \varepsilon). Recall from surreal rate calculus:

\Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3 \qquad (\text{mass-gap dissipation, positive infinitesimal}),
\Omega_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-1} \qquad (\text{Reeb-period budget, positive transfinite}).

Each problem identifies a drift \delta that measures the standard-real deviation from the classical stable configuration. The surreal squeeze delivers the identical inequality:

\delta^2 \cdot \Omega_q > \Delta_q \qquad (\text{in } \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon) \subset \mathbf{No}).

Expanding \Omega_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-1} and \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3: for every standard real \delta > 0, \delta^2 \cdot \varepsilon^{-1} > \varepsilon^3.

See Table 1.

The first three rows are unconditional surreal translations of existing QOU propositions (collapse of the quantum gap, blowup as lifting obstruction, q-Collatz). The fourth row is conditional on P vs NP in the QOU. The fifth row is conditional on q-BSD; the adelic refinement (adelic--Tate surreal squeeze) localises this row at each prime. The sixth row is unconditional once the QOU substrate is posited: the mass gap is a categorical invariant of \mathbf{C} with \ordw(\Delta_q) = -3, and Yang--Mills on \mathbb{R}^4 is the standard part of the q-deformation.

The Navier--Stokes row is a different inference, not a sixth instance of the same one. Five rows follow the schema above: a hypothetical standard-real drift \delta > 0 would cost more than the budget, so no such drift can persist, so \delta = 0 and the conjecture holds. The Navier--Stokes row does not. Its cost column carries no \delta at all — the enstrophy ceiling \mathcal{Z}_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-4/3} is a fixed rate, and the inequality \mathcal{Z}_q > \Delta_q is, in the words of the row's own source block (surreal bound for Navier--Stokes), "automatic". Nothing is being forbidden; a production rate is being compared to an absorption rate, and the conclusion is that the excess is unabsorbed, i.e. that the event occurs.

Both patterns are individually coherent — hypothetical cost exceeds budget, therefore forbidden and production exceeds absorption, therefore singular — but they are not the same argument, and the sentence below about "identifying the problem-specific drift \delta and translating the classical statement into the vanishing of this drift" describes only the first. It does not cover the Navier--Stokes row, whose drift is not asserted to vanish. Read the table as five instances of a squeeze plus one rate comparison sharing a notation, not as six instances of one theorem.

The mass-gap scaling \Delta_q \asymp \varepsilon^3 is a fixed structural invariant of the rigid braided monoidal category \mathbf{C}. It remains constant across problems. The Reeb-period scaling \Omega_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-1} is similarly a fixed structural invariant of the Reeb derivation \xi (categorical Reeb derivation). The content of each millennium problem resides in identifying the problem-specific drift \delta and translating the classical statement into the vanishing of this drift. Once \delta is identified, the squeeze \delta^2 / \varepsilon > \varepsilon^3 closes the argument uniformly.

The six millennium problems are not independent questions but six instances of a single substrate-stability requirement: the observable universe contains only classical-limit configurations where no standard-real drift absorbs more substrate energy than the mass gap dissipates. The Riemann hypothesis is the spectral instance, Navier--Stokes is the hydrodynamic instance, Collatz is the arithmetic instance, P vs NP is the complexity instance, BSD is the elliptic-curve instance, and Yang--Mills is the gauge-theory instance. The adelic--Tate framework (adelic--Tate surreal squeeze) localises each instance at every prime, rendering the squeeze strictly local-global.

The \omega-adic form of each squeeze is registered in the body asymptotics catalog under the \ordw-entry of the corresponding body block (Big-O via \ordw). These remarks can be read in either the "\delta^2 \cdot \Omega_q > \Delta_q in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon)" register or the "\ordw(\text{cost}) > \ordw(\text{budget})" register. The two are equivalent by the Big-O bridge.

rem:algebraic-core-survives: Remark The algebraic core of QOU lifts to any real-closed field. Archimedean specialisation. This survey justifies the central move: the substrate parameter q \in \mathbf{No} may be taken in the infinitesimal neighbourhood of 1, without disturbing any algebraic machinery of this paper. The bulk of the formal structure is purely algebraic. It depends only on the ground ring being a field (typically of characteristic zero), independent of any analytic or topological property of \mathbb{R} or \mathbb{C}.
def:ecalle-borel-resummation: Definition Écalle–Borel resummation: the Borel transform \mathcal{B} and its lateral and median sums. Archimedean specialisation. A divergent Gevrey-1 asymptotic series acquires a canonical analytic meaning through the Borel transform and its Laplace–Borel sums [ecalle1981].
rem:analytic-obstructions: Remark Analytic obstructions: what breaks under surreal replacement. Archimedean specialisation. A first pass at a surreal lift of QOU would catalogue the general-purpose obstructions — Lebesgue measure, Hilbert-space completion, hyperbolic geometry — that surreal numbers famously lack [alling1987]. An honest audit of the actual QOU content, however, finds that most of these obstructions are not triggered by the main paper. This remark records which obstructions genuinely bite and which are only apparent.

rem:ecalle-borel-resurgence-vocabulary: Remark Surrounding resurgence vocabulary and the three "Borel"s. Archimedean specialisation. The operators below are not part of the Écalle–Borel resummation object; they are its surrounding resurgence vocabulary [ecalle1981], together with a disambiguation of the three unrelated "Borel"s in this paper.
prop:habiro-tail-archimedean-action:
Proposition Archimedean \rho_\infty Habiro-tail action of 4_1 is \pi^2/5 (golden-ratio dilogarithm), distinct from the geometric \mathrm{Vol} face. Archimedean specialisation. Conditional on the standard dilogarithm functional equations. Let S(q) = \sum_{n\ge 0} \prod_{j=1}^{n}(1-q^{j})(1-q^{-j}) be the 4_1 Kashaev–Habiro cyclotomic tail, evaluated at real q = e^{t} (the archimedean \rho_\infty face). Then:

  1. S is bar-even: S(q) = S(q^{-1}), since each factor (1-q^{j})(1-q^{-j}) is invariant under q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}.
  2. S is an alternating asymptotic series with (1-q^{j})(1-q^{-j}) = -4\sinh^{2}(jt/2); its optimal-truncation (minimal-term) resurgent action is 
      A_0 \;=\; -4\int_{0}^{\ln\varphi}\ln\!\bigl(2\sinh s\bigr)\,ds \;=\; \frac{\pi^{2}}{5},
    where \varphi = (1+\sqrt5)/2 is the golden ratio and the minimal term sits at \mathrm{arcsinh}(1/2) = \ln\varphi.

The evaluation reduces to the golden-ratio Landen dilogarithm value \mathrm{Li}_2(\varphi^{-2}) = \pi^{2}/15 - \ln^{2}\varphi, one of the classical closed-form values listed in [zagier-dilogarithm, §1]. It follows from Euler reflection, duplication, and Landen's identity at the golden points \psi+\psi^{2}=1, 1+\psi=\varphi, \psi/(1+\psi)=\psi^{2} (with \psi=\varphi^{-1}). Those three functional equations are recalled in [hakimoglu-brown2025, §1.1], whose own golden-ratio result is a different identity (\pi^2/100 as the real part of \mathrm{Li}_2 at a root of a quartic, §6).

Two faces of the same quantum object. The 4_1 quantum dilogarithm admits two distinct archimedean evaluations, which do not coincide:

Face Evaluation Trace field Resurgent action
Geometric / state-integral Faddeev \Phi_b at the substrate b (root-of-unity / Kashaev) \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\pi \approx 0.646
Archimedean \rho_\infty real-q Habiro tail S(q) \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5) \pi^{2}/5 \approx 1.974

The classical dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2 is the semiclassical (b\to 0) leading term of \Phi_b in both cases, but at different arguments — the geometric shape e^{i\pi/3} (giving \mathrm{Vol}, in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})) versus the golden ratio \varphi^{-2} (giving \pi^{2}/5, in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)). That the two faces carry different actions in different number fields is the \hbar \leftrightarrow 2\pi i/N resummation wall made exact: the state-integral and real-q Habiro evaluations are related by resummation, not by term-by-term reparametrisation.

Scope. This is a rigorous statement about the archimedean \rho_\infty (real-q) face. Because S is bar-even, the 4_1 Habiro tail carries no bar-odd datum, consistent with 4_1 amphichirality; the bar-odd (chiral) resurgence relevant to the Q_\beta odd channel must come from a chiral knot such as 5_2. Whether the real-q face — as opposed to the geometric state-integral face — is the physically relevant \rho_\infty evaluation for the Q_\beta observable is an open question; this proposition asserts only the mathematical identity, not a physical identification.

Relation to the proved resurgence results. The standard dictionary behind item 2 runs from a Habiro-ring element \Phi_K to the formal series F_K(x) = \Phi_K(e^{-1/x}) \in \mathbb{C}[[1/x]], its Borel transform G_K, and the median resummation S^{\mathrm{med}}_K; the Costin--Garoufalidis conjecture asks that G_K be resurgent, that S^{\mathrm{med}}_K be analytic on \mathrm{Re}\,x > 0 with radial limits at \tfrac{1}{2\pi i}\mathbb{Q}, and that those limits recover \Phi_K at roots of unity [crew2023, §1, eqs. (1.3)--(1.8) and Conj. 1.1]. Crew, Fantini, Goswami, Osburn and Wheeler prove the resurgence and median-resummation statements for Habiro elements that come from radial limits of partial theta series through a strange identity [crew2023, Thm. 1.2], and deduce the conjecture for the torus-knot families T(2,2u+1) and T(3,2^k) [crew2023, Cor. 1.5 and §3]. The hyperbolic knot 4_1 is not in that class, and the source supplies no strange identity for its tail, so the proved resurgence does not transfer to item 2: the action A_0 = \pi^2/5 above is an optimal-truncation statement about the real-q series and is not a consequence of [crew2023].

The state-integral face in the literature. The geometric face of the table is treated on the q-difference side by Garoufalidis and Wheeler, who work out the 4_1 equation tq\,f(qt;q) + (1-2t)\,f(t;q) + tq^{-1} f(q^{-1}t;q) = 0 completely: its solutions at t = 0 and t = \infty, their monodromy, residues and determinants, the associated state integral, the x-deformation, and an analytic lift of the colored Jones polynomial [garoufalidis-wheeler-modular, §1.5, Thm. 1.7, and \S§5.1--5.8]. That treatment concerns the state-integral face only; it makes no statement about the real-q tail S(q) of item 2.

Extension across the double-twist family. For the double-twist knots K(m,-p) (m,p \ge 1, with K(1,-1) = 4_1), the Lauridsen cyclotomic expansion and the q-hypergeometric Kontsevich--Zagier / strongly-unimodal root-of-unity dualities F_{m,p}(\zeta_N) = U_{m,p}(-1;\zeta_N^{-1}) and \mathcal{F}_{m,p}(\zeta_N) = \mathcal{U}_{m,p}(-1;\zeta_N^{-1}) of Lovejoy and Osburn [lovejoy-osburn, Thms. 1.1--1.2, Cors. 1.3--1.4, eq. (1.2)] write the real-q Habiro tail as \sum_{n\ge 0} C_{K(m,-p),n}(q)\prod_{j=1}^n (1-q^j)(1-q^{-j}). Under q \mapsto q^{-1} the Gaussian q-binomial chains swap m and p, giving C_{K(m,-p),n}(q^{-1}) = C_{K(p,-m),n}(q): bar-evenness therefore holds for the entire amphichiral diagonal K(m,-m) (including 8_3 = K(2,-2)), whereas off-diagonal knots such as 6_1 = K(1,-2) acquire a non-zero bar-odd part and asymmetric q > 1 versus q < 1 optimal-truncation actions. Unlike bar-evenness, the golden-ratio action \pi^2/5 is specific to the m = p = 1 base case where C_{K(1,-1),n}(q) = 1: on the q > 1 ray of K(2,-1) = 6_1^* (equivalently q < 1 of 6_1) the q^{n_1^2 + n_1} weight shifts the dilogarithm saddle to \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2}) at e^{u^*} = 1 + 1/\sqrt{2}, giving the exact octagonal action \pi^2/8, whereas the q > 1 ray of 6_1 (A_0^+ \approx 1.6433) and the amphichiral knot 8_3 = K(2,-2) (A_0 \approx 0.9913, distinct from \mathrm{Vol}(8_3)/\pi \approx 1.6648) are governed by a quartic inner saddle whose optimal-truncation actions are \mathbb{Q}-linearly independent of \pi^2 up to norm 10^4.
def:standard-part-functor:
Definition standard-part map \mathrm{st} : \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} \to \mathbb{R}. Archimedean specialisation. The standard-part map realizes the quotient \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} / \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{inf}} \cong \mathbb{R} and underlies the classical limit at q = 1 + \varepsilon; its construction begins with the finite and infinitesimal surreals.

An element x \in \mathbf{No} is finite if there exists n \in \mathbb{N} with |x| \leq n. Write \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} \subset \mathbf{No} for the subring of finite surreals, and \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{inf}} \subset \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} for the ideal of infinitesimals (those x with |x| < 1/n for every n \in \mathbb{N}).
rem:st-is-median-resummation:
Remark The standard-part map acts as Écalle median resummation on transseries values. Archimedean specialisation. The standard-part map \mathrm{st} (standard-part functor) and the median resummation \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{med}} of Écalle–Borel resummation compute the same value wherever both are defined. This remark records the identification once, at block level; elsewhere it appears only in passing inside the surreal Kashaev reformulation.

Concretely: let \tilde f be a Gevrey-1 transseries whose Borel transform admits lateral Laplace sums along a Stokes ray. The two lateral sums \mathcal{L}^{\theta^\pm}\tilde f disagree by exponentially small terms; the median sum \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{med}}\tilde f is the unique real single-valued average. On the surreal side, the same \tilde f is a transseries in the sense of Berarducci–Mantova [berarducci-mantova2018], hence evaluates at a positive infinitesimal (or, for asymptotic-in-n series, at n = \omega) to a finite element of \mathbf{No}, and \mathrm{st} projects that element to \mathbb{R}. Selecting the real single-valued representative is precisely what \mathrm{st} does to the finite surreal value:

  \mathrm{st}\bigl(\tilde f\,\big|_{\,\varepsilon}\bigr)
  \;=\; \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{med}}\tilde f ,

read as an identity of the two selection rules, not as a new theorem: each side is the unique real, single-valued value compatible with the asymptotics of \tilde f (Watson/Nevanlinna–Sokal uniqueness supplies the analytic half; the valuation quotient \mathcal{O}/\mathfrak{m} \cong \mathbb{R} supplies the surreal half). A concrete class on which median resummation is proved to exist: for elements of the Habiro ring that arise from partial theta series through strange identities, the Borel transform of the associated series is resurgent, and its median resummation is analytic on \mathrm{Re}(x) > 0 with radial limits at the points \tfrac{1}{2\pi i}\mathbb{Q} of its natural boundary [crew2023, Thm. 1.2]. A second class: for the holomorphic quantum modular forms g of their Types 4 and 5, g equals the median resummation \mathcal{S}^{\pi/2}_{\mathrm{med}} of its asymptotic expansion at a rational point -d/c [mcspirit-rolen2025, §3.2].

A second condition for transseries. Watson/Nevanlinna–Sokal uniqueness is a statement about one Borel-summable series. A transseries \Phi = \sum_{\ell} y^{\ell}\,\varphi_{\ell}(g) is a sum over non-perturbative sectors, and its lateral resummation s_{\pm}(\Phi) = \sum_{\ell} y^{\ell}\,s_{\pm}(\varphi_{\ell})(g) is itself an infinite sum that can diverge. Reorganising by fixed power n of the coupling gives the partial series G_n(y) = \sum_{\ell} a_{n,\ell}\,y^{\ell}; when all the G_n converge with a common radius R, the resummed transseries is a well-defined function [arxiv-2302.08363v2, §2]. The identification above therefore uses, for a transseries \tilde f, this convergence of partial series in addition to one-series uniqueness. For the figure-eight complement the Andersen–Kashaev state integral is written there as a lateral Borel resummation of an explicit transseries with two instanton towers whose action is the hyperbolic volume V = 2.029883\ldots; the partial series factorise as G^{i}_n(y) = a_n M_i(y) with M_{1,2} convergent of radius 1, so every partial series converges with the same radius [arxiv-2302.08363v2, §4]. Whether the transseries of the substrate satisfies the same common-radius condition is not checked here.

Three consequences:

  1. Directionality of the citation graph. Resurgence-side blocks and witnesses (the alien datum, Borel-singularity probes, saddle transseries) may cite this result when they take a real value of a resummed series; the surreal appendix no longer needs to restate the analytic machinery.
  2. The Kashaev application. In the surreal Kashaev statement the map \mathrm{st} applied to 2\pi \log |J_K(\zeta_\omega, \omega)| / \omega is the median resummation of the Kashaev transseries at the root of unity — the asymptotic-limit content of the volume conjecture in resummation form.
  3. Scope. The identification is language-level: it names one operation consistently across the two vocabularies. It does not enlarge the class of summable series and does not touch the genuinely geometric inputs (hyperbolic volume).
rem:standard-part-classical-limit:
Remark Standard-part as the exact classical-limit substitute. Archimedean specialisation. ## Example: Jackson derivative

The Jackson derivative

  d_q f(x) = \frac{f(qx) - f(x)}{(q - 1) x}

at q = 1 + \varepsilon has birthday \leq \omega + 1 (the coefficients are rational in \varepsilon). Applying \mathrm{st} recovers the classical derivative exactly:

  \mathrm{st}\!\bigl(d_{1 + \varepsilon} f(x_0)\bigr) = \frac{df}{dx}(x_0)
  \qquad (x_0 \in \mathbb{R}).

This is the exact substitute for the (broken) classical-limit functor (classical limit functor): instead of taking q \to 1 as a topological limit in \mathbb{R}, evaluate at a specific infinitesimal-shifted surreal and take the standard-part. Unlike the topological limit, this construction makes sense in pure algebra.
rem:archimedean-functor-trace-commutativ:
Remark Archimedean realisation and binding-trace commutativity. Archimedean specialisation. ## Archimedean realisation & Trace Commutativity

Two independently defined binding traces — the exact active-partition factorization B_{\mathrm{sym}} and the Q-CLT statistical limit B_{\mathrm{qCLT}} — must land on the same macroscopic observable, and the standard-part map is what guarantees it. Here \mathcal{F}_{Arch} denotes the object-level standard-part map \mathrm{st} \colon \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} \to \mathbb{R} — a surjective ring homomorphism — applied to the real-valued binding traces; it is the underlying evaluation of the categorical standard-part functor \mathrm{St} (def:standard-part-functor), not a functor in its own right. It transforms algebraic traces into physical macroscopic observables, so that the evaluation of nuclear binding traces rigorously commutes as the scale A \to \infty. The payoff is already concrete in the tritium / helium-3 splitting: both routes agree that the n–n bond of tritium binds more tightly than the p–p bond of helium-3.

conj:diophantine-birthday:
Conjecture Algebraic vs transcendental numbers are separated by birthday trajectory. Archimedean specialisation. Liouville's theorem and Roth's theorem bound the approximability of an algebraic irrational by rationals: if \alpha is algebraic of degree d, then |\alpha - p/q| > c/q^d for sufficiently large q (Liouville), and Roth improves the exponent to 2 + \delta for any \delta > 0. Use \delta rather than \varepsilon here to avoid collision with the surreal infinitesimal \varepsilon = 1/\omega used elsewhere in this appendix.

These are analytic statements about approximation rates. The surreal framework suggests a direct algebraic shadow. Algebraic and transcendental numbers distinguish themselves by the birthday trajectory of their sign sequences (birthday grading).
thm:diophantine-birthday-trajectory:
Theorem The birthday-trajectory separation: impossible at the birthday, unobstructed at the trajectory, and blocked only by a quantifier. Archimedean specialisation. ## What "separated by birthday trajectory" can and cannot mean

The appendix carries a conjecture that algebraic and transcendental numbers are separated by birthday trajectory, motivated by Liouville and Roth. Taken literally as a statement about the birthday of the number, it is not open — it is impossible.

The axiom \mathrm{birthday}(\iota r) \le \omega places every real, algebraic and transcendental alike, inside [0,\omega]. In Conway's surreals the collapse is total: the dyadic rationals are born strictly before day \omega and every other real is born exactly on day \omega, so

  \mathrm{birthday}(\sqrt{2}) \;=\; \omega \;=\; \mathrm{birthday}(\pi).

Two numbers with equal birthday are indistinguishable to every predicate of the birthday, so no criterion phrased in \mathrm{birthday} \circ \iota can separate them, however cleverly chosen.

The conjecture's own wording already said where to look. Trajectory is load-bearing: Liouville and Roth are about how fast rationals approximate \alpha, which in surreal terms is the shape of the sign expansion — the path — not the ordinal at which it terminates.
conj:infinitesimal-frobenius: Conjecture Infinitesimal Frobenius pairing: \int_A \circ \mu = \mathrm{id} + O(\varepsilon). Archimedean specialisation. The Frobenius axiom in quantum observable universe requires the pairing \int_A \circ \mu : A \otimes A \to \mathbf{1} to induce an isomorphism A \xrightarrow{\sim} A^{\vee} — a strict equality, hence a binary non-degeneracy condition. Over the surreals this condition can fail at infinitesimal scale, where a pairing may be non-degenerate only up to an infinitesimal correction. Two phenomena already invite such a reading — the diagonal regularisation of the Möbius energy and the small residual error in the QOU mass formula's \mathcal{Q}-values (quantified in §Significance below) — each of which the sections below interpret as an infinitesimal Frobenius deviation. In a surreal QOU, the strict axiom can accordingly be relaxed.
conj:surreal-limit-transfer:
Conjecture Surreal limit transfer: limits as standard-part equalities via an \omega-evaluation. Archimedean specialisation. There is an \omega-evaluation \mathrm{ev}_\omega : \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbf{No} of real sequences, sending constants to their embedded reals, respecting pointwise addition and multiplication, transferring eventual pointwise domination to the surreal order, and evaluating every convergent sequence infinitesimally close to its limit:

  a_n \to L
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathrm{ev}_\omega(a) - L \in \mathfrak{m},
  \qquad
  \mathrm{st}\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_\omega(a)\bigr) = L .

Here \mathfrak{m} is the infinitesimal ideal of the finite valuation ring (valuation ring of finite surreals) and \mathrm{st} the standard-part map.

This is the block-level home for the "move analytic \to surreal" operation: an analytic limit statement becomes a surreal equality up to an infinitesimal — and, after \mathrm{st}, an exact equality. Two consequences are derived, fully proved, from the hypotheses of the conjecture:

  1. Limits are computed by \mathrm{st} \circ \mathrm{ev}_\omega .
  2. Limit comparison: if a_n \le b_n eventually and both converge, then \lim a_n \le \lim b_n — the eventual inequality is transferred to a single surreal inequality at \omega and the archimedean conclusion recovered by the proved monotonicity of \mathrm{st}. The classical strict-inequality collapse is visible structurally: \mathrm{ev}_\omega(a) < \mathrm{ev}_\omega(b) is compatible with equal standard parts, so only \le survives the wall.
conj:on-p-modular-hecke:
Conjecture Modular Hecke at q = \zeta_p corresponds to nimber surreals \mathbf{On}_p. Archimedean specialisation. This conjecture extends, to a primitive p-th root of unity, the char-0 surreal picture of Hecke representation theory recalled next. Hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction identifies the binary \{L \mid R\} split at each Hecke eigenchannel step with Conway's recursive surreal construction. This works because the Hecke generator \sigma has exactly two eigenvalues at generic q.

At a primitive p-th root of unity q = \zeta_p, the representation theory of H_n(\zeta_p) acquires p-ary structure: when \geq p copies of the fundamental representation V are tensored, certain summands in the q-Schur--Weyl decomposition become trivial (Lusztig's small quantum group \mathfrak{u}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) is finite-dimensional, with truncation governed by p).

This conjecture asserts the natural extension of Hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction to the modular setting: the modular Hecke combinatorics at q = \zeta_p corresponds to nimber surreals \mathbf{On}_p in characteristic p (Lenstra--Conway).

conj:wenzl-positivity-implies-substrate-:
Conjecture Wenzl positivity at q_0 implies substrate C^*-Frobenius positivity. Archimedean specialisation. The companion conjecture Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2 reduces the Wightman-axiom portion of the Yang–Mills millennium statement to a single substrate axiom: C^*-Frobenius positivity of the QOU Frobenius–Hopf substrate at q = q_0. This conjecture takes the natural next step. The axiom should be derivable from Wenzl's positivity criterion for \mathrm{Rep}(U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)) at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1}, as a consequence of existing unitarity.

Conjecture (Wenzl positivity at q_0 implies substrate C^*-Frobenius positivity). Wenzl's positivity criterion for the representation category \mathrm{Rep}(U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)) at q = q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1} — the criterion that picks out unitary fusion categories among the q-deformed semisimple ones — implies the substrate C^*-Frobenius positivity axiom of Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2. Equivalently, the Müger C^*-norm on the Frobenius–Hopf substrate A at q_0, induced by the categorical trace of \mathrm{Rep}(U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)), makes the antipode-twisted Frobenius pairing \langle\theta(\cdot), \cdot\rangle_F positive-definite on the positive-time Reeb half.

Here \theta is the Reeb reflection (the antipodal \mathbb{Z}_2 \subset U(1) of Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity from the Reeb \mathbb{Z}_2) and \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_F the Frobenius form of A.

sec:surreal-appendix-conclusion:
Open questions and outlook.

The surreal-number lift of QOU raises several questions:

  1. Surreal measure? The category \mathbf{No} carries no canonical Lebesgue measure. Loeb-type constructions on hyperfinite subsets of \mathbf{No} yield finitely additive measures that pull back to \mathbb{R} under the standard part. Whether such a construction recovers the Frobenius integral \int_A up to an infinitesimal is left open.
  2. Surreal Hilbert-like object. The scattering pipeline's Hilbert space \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{phys}} lacks a surreal analogue with a canonical inner product. Whether a birthday-bounded completion yields a weaker surrogate—sufficient for the mass formula but lacking spectral theory—remains to be investigated.
  3. Categorical size. Since \mathbf{No} is a proper class, defining \mathbf{Mod}_{\mathbf{No}} or \mathbf{Rep}_{\mathbf{No}}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) requires universe-polymorphic foundations or restriction to a set-sized Hahn-series sub-field. This is sidestepped by stating axioms over a fixed real-closed field K extending \mathbb{R}.
  4. Genuine generalisations. The strict QOU axioms (\int \circ \eta = \mathrm{id}, \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0) might force the \varepsilon-relaxed versions to coincide with the strict ones in any rigid monoidal category. If so, the \varepsilon-flexibility is illusory.
  5. Kashaev as a surreal statement. The reformulation \mathrm{st}\bigl(2 \pi \log |J_K(q_\omega, \omega)|/\omega\bigr) = \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) (Kashaev surreal) is equivalent to the classical conjecture, modulo the meaning of q_\omega. It separates the algebraic (Hecke/Markov) content from the transcendental (dilogarithm, hyperbolic volume) content.

Accomplishments of this appendix:

  • An explicit ambient for the q \to 1 limit and renormalisation blow-ups, avoiding informal \infty notation.
  • An isomorphism between the Hoefsmit seminormal form (central to the mass formula) and Conway's \{L \mid R\} construction.
  • A disciplined framework for \varepsilon-relaxed axioms.
  • A catalogue of which QOU constructions are purely algebraic (hence field-polymorphic) versus genuinely analytic.

This appendix serves as raw material for future work rather than a completed extension of the theory.
